summary: Comprehensive backend + frontend E2E testing of BITLOGIC. Backend: 20/22 tests pass (91%). Frontend: All critical flows verified (admin login, config, add student, create puzzle, student login, dashboard gate & rounds, Round 1 submit, leaderboard).

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout is unreliable. `request.client.host` returns the k8s ingress pod IP (which rotates), so identifier `ip:email` differs across requests and the count rarely reaches 5 for the same combination. Test observed lockout (429) triggered once then reverted to 401 on subsequent attempts. Should use X-Forwarded-For / real client IP, or key lockout by email only.

minor.issue: Occasional 502/HTML response when creating many students in rapid succession from finalize test (JSONDecodeError). Appears to be transient ingress issue; not consistently reproducible. Consider batching or rate-limit hardening.

Successful register does not clear login_attempts for that email; also failed login always resets locked_until forward on every attempt effectively extending lockout indefinitely as long as attacker keeps trying.

issues: scratch.mit.edu sets X-Frame-Options=sameorigin so iframe never renders; only a blank frame appears. Consider showing a fallback link or a message telling users to open Scratch in a new tab. Element exists as required per spec.

action_items: Fix brute-force lockout: use X-Forwarded-For real client IP or key by email only; also clear login_attempts on successful register/reset.
Consider a fallback UI when scratch.mit.edu refuses to be framed (open-in-new-tab button).
critical_code_review_comments: Auth lockout `check_lockout` relies on `request.client.host` which behind k8s ingress is the pod IP, defeating the lockout.

In login failure path, `locked_until` is unconditionally overwritten on every attempt; if you also increment past 5, the lockout keeps extending on every wrong try (annoying but acceptable). Fine as-is.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend tests must be run non-parallel (-o addopts=) because they mutate shared competition config. Existing test file at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py covers all endpoints. Main gap: brute-force lockout bug + finalize test occasionally flaky under load.
rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout keys the counter by `request.client.host + email`. Behind the Kubernetes ingress, `request.client.host` is the ingress proxy IP (not the true client), and the environment routes different requests through different upstream connections leading to varying `client.host` values. Result: the counter is spread across several identifiers and rarely accumulates to the 5-attempt threshold for a real attacker. Mitigation: parse `X-Forwarded-For` (first hop) or key the lockout by email only (with an admin exclusion) or by hashed identifier of email+first-XFF.
